text:
US AI is generating far more revenue than Chinese AI:

As of the end of September, OpenAI and Anthropic had a combined estimated annualized revenue run rate of $105 billion.

This is nearly 10 times the $11 billion generated by 6 Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek, Z Dot ai, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax.

ByteDance accounted for 36% of this figure at $4 billion.

In Q3 alone, Anthropic's sales grew +47% QoQ, to a record $17 billion.

At the same time, OpenAI revenue surged +50% to a record $10 billion.

By comparison, DeepSeek's annualized revenue run rate doubled in September, but stands at just $1 billion.

US tech firms remain in the lead of the AI race.

en_summary: You could get paid $1,230 today on 100 shares of $AMD you already own via a covered call, with $AMD trading around $582.
text:
You could get paid $1,230 today on 100 shares of $AMD you already own.

It's called a covered call, and here's how it works:

$AMD trades around $582, so 100 shares are worth about $58,200. You sell one $700 call expiring December 18 and collect about $12.30 a share, or $1,230, up front. That strike is about 20% above today's price.

In exchange, you agree to sell your 100 shares at $700 if AMD is above that price on December 18.

At expiration, one of two things happens:

1. $AMD finishes below $700. The call expires worthless. You keep the $1,230 and your shares, a 2.1% return in 36 days, and you're free to sell another call.

2. $AMD finishes above $700. Your shares are sold at $700. That's an $11,805 gain from today's price plus the $1,230 premium, or $13,035 in total (22.4%).

You don't have to wait until expiration either. I usually buy the call back once it has lost about half its value, then sell the next one.

The catch: your upside stops at $700. If $AMD runs to $800, the gains above $700 go to the call buyer. The premium also doesn't protect you much on the way down. It only cushions $12.30 a share, so your breakeven from today's price is $569.65.

$AMD isn't expected to report earnings again until after December 18, so there's no earnings report inside this trade.

Only sell a call at a strike where you'd be happy to sell your shares.

Not financial advice. I share these for education.

The Claude AI developer is seeking $64.4 billion through its IPO, plus a $26 billion private placement, potentially raising a combined $90.4 billion in a record-breaking offering.

Nvidia ($NVDA) has committed approximately $10 billion to the private placement, despite its recent stock selloff.

Demand is soaring even at a targeted $1.4 trillion valuation, with some investors expected to receive reduced allocations.

OUSTED NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG LINKED TO THIRD AFFAIR, REUTERS REPORTS

Former Nvidia ($NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with another company employee, according to two sources cited by Reuters.

The revelation follows two previously reported affairs involving Nvidia healthcare VP Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang, a Chinese executive suspected by US intelligence of espionage.

The earlier scandals reportedly led to Huang’s resignation on November 12.

Nvidia declined to comment, while Huang and the company’s board did not respond to Reuters’ requests.
